name: 01-showcase-hero
title: The public showcase, at the top of the page
purpose: The only screen a visitor sees before signing in. It calls no API, so no stock, price or customer data appears here.

callouts.label: The brand mark. It links to the catalogue once you are signed in, and to this page while you are not
The navigation tray. While signed out it holds Home and Collection only
Language selector
Sign in opens the login page
The opening line of the showcase
Explore the collection goes straight to the catalogue, where you still have to sign in

name: 02-showcase-end
title: The end of the showcase
purpose: The scroll scene ends on a closing panel and a footer, so the way into the shop is never more than a scroll away.

callouts.label: Open the catalogue is the main route into the shop
Sign in and Create account are repeated here so a reader who scrolled past the header is not stuck

name: 03-sign-in
title: Signing in
purpose: Every screen except this showcase needs an account, because live stock is treated as commercial information.

callouts.label: Your email address, exactly as it was registered
Your password. It is never shown in the address bar or stored in the browser beyond the session
Sign in. The button reads Signing in… while the request is in flight and cannot be pressed twice
New customer? Create an account

name: 04-register
title: Creating a customer account
purpose: Self-registration always creates a Customer. Staff, Inventory and Administrator logins are made by an Administrator on the Administration screen.

callouts.label: Your full name, as it will appear on orders and invoices
Email address, which is also your login
A password of at least 8 characters
Create account

name: 05-catalogue
title: The catalogue
purpose: The working screen for a customer: live availability straight from stock, with the server as the source of truth for every quantity.

callouts.label: The tab you are on is filled with the amber selection colour, the same look the open account menu and the switched-on theme take
Your role’s tabs. A customer sees Products and My Orders
Cart, notification bell and account menu live in this group
Search by product name or SKU. It waits 300 ms after you stop typing
The category tree with product counts. Clicking a branch filters the grid
Availability, price range and sort live in the same panel
A product card. The chips under the name are shortcuts that apply that filter
The stock badge: In stock, Low stock with the count left, Out of stock or Inactive. It carries a glyph and a word, never colour alone
The quantity stepper cannot be raised above what is in stock

name: 06-cart
title: The cart and checkout
purpose: The cart lives in your browser until you place the order. Stock is only reserved at that moment, which is the first point where the promise can actually be kept.

callouts.label: Each line shows the unit price and what is available right now
The stepper per line, capped at live stock
Remove takes just that line out
Total, priced in the store currency
Place order sends the whole basket as one request with an idempotency key

name: 07-my-orders
title: My orders
purpose: Every order on the account with its current status, and the printable invoice for each.

callouts.label: Filter by status. The list is paged at ten orders
A row: order number, when it was placed, how many items, the total and where it is now
View opens the order with its timeline
Invoice opens the printable version

name: 08-order-detail
title: One order, start to finish
purpose: The timeline says exactly where the order is, and the sentence under it says what that status means for you.

callouts.label: The current status
Pending, Confirmed, Shipped, or the terminal Rejected or Cancelled
Printable invoice
The lines as they were bought, with the price the server charged at that moment
Cancel order releases the reserved stock. It is offered only while the order is Pending or Confirmed

name: 09-invoice
title: The invoice
purpose: A single page you can print or save as PDF. Printing always uses white paper, whatever theme you read it in.

callouts.label: Print calls the browser’s own print dialog
Billed to
Payment is handled outside this system, and the invoice says so rather than implying it was taken
Line items with quantity, unit price and amount

name: 10-dashboard
title: Your dashboard
purpose: The account summary: what you have ordered, what it cost, and what needs your attention.

callouts.label: Total orders, total spent, active orders and delivered, counted from your own orders
Shortcuts to the three pages a customer uses
Orders by status. Shipped means in transit here; delivery confirmation is a separate status this system does not have
Edit profile

name: 11-profile
title: Profile, password and addresses
purpose: Your contact details, the password you sign in with, and the delivery addresses checkout offers.

callouts.label: Name and phone. Your email is the login, so it is shown but not editable
Save changes
Change password asks for the current one first, and rates the strength of the new one

name: 11b-addresses
title: Saved delivery addresses
purpose: The address book checkout offers, on the same profile page below the password card.

callouts.label: Saved delivery addresses. The default one is offered at checkout
The form below the list adds an address; Save address keeps it for the next order

name: 12-notifications
title: Notifications
purpose: Order updates for everyone, plus new-order and low-stock messages for staff.

callouts.label: Filter the inbox: All, Unread, Orders, Promotions
Mark all as read
The inbox: what changed, when, and a link to the order it is about. Ticking rows makes Mark as read and Delete apply to the selection
Preferences. Order notices are always on; promotions can be muted per channel, with quiet hours

name: 13-staff-console
title: The staff order console
purpose: Staff move orders through the lifecycle. They cannot create products or touch stock - that is the Inventory Manager’s job.

callouts.label: A staff member’s tabs: Products, Orders, Sales
The three queues a staff member works through: To confirm, To ship, and Invoices & history
Switch between the order list and category management
The queue you are in: every order still Pending, oldest first
Confirm accepts the order and keeps the stock reserved
Reject declines it and releases the reserved stock back to the shelf
Tick rows to confirm or reject a batch at once

name: 14-sales-summary
title: Sales summary
purpose: Read-only reporting over every order. Cancelled and rejected orders are counted but bring in no revenue.

callouts.label: From and To are calendar days in your own time zone, converted to UTC at the edges
Apply range
Orders, revenue and the range you asked for

name: 14b-sales-breakdown
title: The same figures as a breakdown
purpose: Below the tiles on the sales page: the charts, and the table behind them with each status’s share.

callouts.label: Orders and revenue by status, drawn as charts
The same numbers as a table, so the report is readable without the chart

name: 13b-category-stock-dark
title: Categories & stock, in the dark theme
purpose: The staff screen has a second half: the category tree, with the stock that sits under each branch. The figures are read from the catalogue and are never edited here.

callouts.label: The staff screen splits in two: the order console and this category manager. The half you are on carries the amber fill
The section heading
The two views: the tree with its stock summary, and the product category and tag editor
Find a category by its own name or its parent’s. It filters as you type and goes back to the first page
Create category opens the same form on an empty record
The summary counts every product in the branch, not only the ones filed directly under it
Category, Products, In stock, Low stock and Manage
One row per category, indented by how deep it sits. An inactive category carries its own badge
Edit opens the category form. Nothing on this screen changes a stock figure

name: 13c-category-editor-dark
title: The category editor, in the dark theme
purpose: Everything that can be done to one category: rename it, change its slug, move it under another parent, reorder it, switch it off and delete it.

callouts.label: The dialog is named after the category, so a screen reader and the address of the request agree
Close dialog. Escape does the same thing and hands focus back to the Edit button you came from
Category name, required, up to 120 characters
The slug used in the address bar, written for you from the name and still editable
Parent category. Choosing another branch is what moves this one
Sort order inside the parent
Active category. Switching it off hides the branch and everything under it from browsing, and leaves stock alone
Save category
Move category reparents on its own. A branch moved under one of its own descendants is refused: "A category cannot move under itself or a descendant."
Reassign products and children to: where the contents go when the category is deleted
Delete category. Greyed out while the category still holds products or children, so nothing is orphaned

name: 13d-product-organization-dark
title: Product categories & tags: choosing the product
purpose: The second view files a product under the categories and tags the catalogue filters on. It is paged at twenty products, the same list the customer browses.

callouts.label: The two views, with this one selected
The heading of the view
Find a product by name or SKU. It waits a quarter of a second after you stop typing
The product, named with its SKU so two similar names cannot be confused
Twenty products to a page; the inventory list pages the same table at fifty
Once a product is chosen its own editor appears below, holding the categories it is filed under today

name: 13e-product-tags-dark
title: Filing a product under categories and tags
purpose: The same screen scrolled to that editor: what a product belongs to, which of those is its primary category, and its tags.

callouts.label: Every category in the tree, indented, with the ones this product is filed under ticked. The list scrolls inside its own box
Primary category: the one the product page marks "· primary" and the order line records. Always one of the ticked ones
Tags, comma separated. The customer’s filter chips are built from these
Save product categories sends the whole set as one request, so a product is never left between two states

name: 15-inventory
title: Inventory
purpose: Where products are created and stock is corrected. Every change is appended to the ledger, and the database refuses to go below zero.

callouts.label: Search by name or SKU
New product. A new product starts at zero stock on purpose - stock arrives through an adjustment so it is audited
Stock and availability per row. Rows at or below the low-stock threshold are marked
Edit opens the product form
Adjust stock opens the signed adjustment
History opens the same dialog on the movement ledger

name: 16-bulk-edit
title: Bulk editing products
purpose: Category, tag, brand and active state can be set for a page of products at once. Stock is never part of a bulk edit - it keeps its atomic, single-product path.

callouts.label: How many products are selected
The action. Stock is deliberately absent from this list
The parameter the action needs: a category, tags, or a brand and series
Review changes opens the confirmation dialog
Clear drops the selection and the bar goes with it

name: 17-bulk-confirm
title: Confirming a bulk edit
purpose: Nothing is written until this dialog is confirmed, and the summary says what will happen.

callouts.label: What is about to change, and to how many products
Products that already match are skipped, so re-running is safe
Apply changes sends one request for the whole selection
Cancel closes it without a request

name: 18-adjust-stock
title: Adjusting stock
purpose: The only way stock changes outside an order, and it always carries a reason.

callouts.label: The product and its current quantity
A signed number: negative for shrinkage or damage, positive for a delivery
Reason is mandatory, and lands in the ledger with your name
Apply adjustment. If it would take the product below zero the server refuses it

name: 18b-movement-history
title: The movement ledger for one product
purpose: The same dialog, scrolled down: every stock change against the product, with who made it and why. A product nobody has touched says so.

callouts.label: The ledger heading. Opening it from a row puts the keyboard focus here, so the history can be read straight away
Movement history for this product: when, by how much, why and who. A product with no movements yet says so

name: 19-admin-users
title: Administration: users
purpose: Administrators create staff logins, change roles and switch accounts off. They are read-only on orders and inventory, so nobody can both sell and silently restock.

callouts.label: The three sections: Users, Audit log, Settings
Create a user: email, password, role, and a name when the role is Customer
Change a role from the row itself. It takes effect on the user’s next request
Deactivate keeps the history and blocks the login. The last active administrator cannot be removed

name: 20-admin-audit
title: Administration: audit log
purpose: What happened, who did it and when. It is the record the concurrency design writes as it goes.

callouts.label: Filter by action prefix, for example order. or user.
When, actor, action, entity and the details of the change

name: 21-admin-settings
title: Administration: settings
purpose: The one business number an administrator can edit.

callouts.label: Low stock threshold. Products at or below it are flagged everywhere in the app, and the inventory rows are marked
Save settings writes it to the database, not to a config file
